title: PPM format and ffmpeg pipeline reference
purpose: Verified facts about the Netpbm PPM format and how ffmpeg ingests it. Every claim here was checked against the vendored ffmpeg source tree or an executed command, not recalled.

source_files: libavcodec/pnm.c -- ff_pnm_decode_header, the actual header parser
libavcodec/pnmdec.c -- sample decoding and maxval scaling
libavcodec/pnm_parser.c -- splits a concatenated stream into frames

why_ppm.rationale: PPM is the lowest-friction way to get pixels out of a program and into a video encoder. The encoder is the only dependency; the format itself needs no library.
properties: Header is plain ASCII, body is raw bytes. A conforming writer is about five lines of code.
No compression, no chunk framing, no checksums, so nothing can be subtly malformed.
Streamable: frames concatenate directly, which is what lets us pipe instead of staging files.
Supported by essentially every image tool, and by ffmpeg as a first-class demuxer.
costs: Uncompressed: width * height * 3 bytes per frame. 1920x1080 is 6.2 MB/frame, ~373 MB/s at 60fps.
No alpha channel. Use PAM (P7) if alpha is genuinely required.
8 bits per channel at maxval 255, so heavy post-grading will band. Use maxval 65535 for 16-bit.

P7.note: keyword header terminated by ENDHDR; supports alpha and 16-bit

PF.note: for HDR output; header carries a scale whose sign encodes endianness

format.use: P6. It is binary (so writing is a single fwrite of the whole frame), it is RGB, and it is the most widely supported.

p6_layout.header: P6 <ws> width <ws> height <ws> maxval <single whitespace byte>
p6_layout.then: width * height * 3 samples, row-major, top row first, R then G then B per pixel
p6_layout.example_header_length:
"P6
64 36
255
" is 13 bytes; header length varies with the digit count, so never hardcode it

rules: Whitespace between header fields is any run of space, LF, CR or TAB (ffmpeg pnm_space()).
Exactly ONE whitespace byte separates maxval from the pixel data. Additional whitespace would be read as pixel data.
A '#' in the header starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. Comments are legal but pointless in generated output, and a '#' appearing in binary pixel data is NOT a comment.
maxval must be > 0 and <= 65535. ffmpeg rejects 0 and anything larger.
maxval <= 255 means one byte per sample. maxval >= 256 means TWO bytes per sample, big-endian.
Rows are written top-to-bottom. This is the opposite of the GLSL/OpenGL convention, which is the single most common source of vertically mirrored output.

maxval_scaling_gotcha.what: ffmpeg rescales samples when maxval is not exactly 255 (or 65535 for 16-bit).
maxval_scaling_gotcha.detail: pnmdec.c computes a fixed-point factor and remaps every sample to the full 8- or 16-bit range. maxval 255 hits the no-op path.
maxval_scaling_gotcha.implication: Always write maxval 255 for 8-bit output. A value like 100 still decodes, but every sample is multiplied, so your bytes are not the bytes ffmpeg sees.

byte_conversion.correct: clamp the float to [0,1] first, then scale: v <= 0 ? 0 : v >= 1 ? 255 : (unsigned char)(v * 255 + 0.5)
byte_conversion.why: An unclamped value above 1.0 wraps modulo 256, so an over-bright highlight becomes a dark speckle. Shaders that tonemap with tanh() rarely exceed 1, but any additive accumulation can, and the artefact looks like sensor noise rather than clipping.
byte_conversion.rounding: The + 0.5 matters: truncation biases every channel down by an average of half a level, which shows up as a slight overall darkening.

file_sequence.how: Write numbered files, then read them with a printf pattern.
pros: Frames are inspectable and re-encodable without re-rendering.
A crashed render leaves usable partial output.
cons: Needs disk space equal to the full uncompressed sequence.
Thousands of file creations; on network or container filesystems this dominates runtime.
file_sequence.pattern_note: %04d must match the zero-padding actually written. %02d will not find frame0000.ppm. Use -start_number if the sequence does not begin at 0.

pipe.how: Write concatenated P6 frames to stdout and pipe them straight into ffmpeg.
pros: Render and encode overlap, so encoding is nearly free in wall-clock terms.
No filename padding to get wrong.
cons: Nothing to inspect afterwards unless you also tee the frames.
A crash loses the whole render.
pipe.how_splitting_works: libavcodec/pnm_parser.c scans for the next 'P6' header and computes each frame's exact byte length from its own width/height/maxval. That is why a bare concatenation of frames -- with no container, no separators, no index -- is a valid stream.
pipe.explicit_f_required: Give -f ppm_pipe explicitly when reading stdin. Probing a pipe is less reliable than probing a file, and the failure mode is a confusing 'invalid data' rather than a clear message.

framerate_flag_placement.rule: -framerate N BEFORE -i sets the INPUT rate. -r N AFTER -i sets the OUTPUT rate and resamples by duplicating or dropping frames.

measured_example.result_a: 72 frames, duration 1.20s -- input decoded at the image2 default of 25fps, then upsampled to 60fps
measured_example.note: This was measured with the vendored build, not inferred. Command A is the form used in most PPM tutorials, including the gist this project started from, and it silently produces a 2.4x frame-duplicated file.

framerate_flag_placement.default_input_rate: 25 fps, from the `framerate` AVOption on the image2/image2pipe demuxers (libavformat/img2dec.c). It is a decode-side option, which is why placement matters.

frame_duplication_on_decode.rule: When decoding to a frame stream, pass -fps_mode passthrough (an OUTPUT option, so after -i). Without it ffmpeg conforms output to a constant rate taken from r_frame_rate and DUPLICATES frames to fill the gaps.
frame_duplication_on_decode.why_it_matters_beyond_speed: The duplicates are byte-identical to their predecessors, so they read as HELD frames. Analysis then reported the sequence as animated 'on twos' with 55% holds, which was a property of our own decode command rather than of the content. After the fix the same clip reads 'on ones' with 8% holds. A measurement pipeline that decodes carelessly will confidently describe its own artefacts.
frame_duplication_on_decode.companion_rule: Use avg_frame_rate, not r_frame_rate, to time the output. r_frame_rate is an upper bound on the timebase; timing 270 frames at 120fps instead of 57.5 would play the result at over twice speed.

demuxer_options.video_size: only needed for headerless raw input; PPM carries its own size
demuxer_options.frame_size: force a fixed frame size in bytes for pipes; not needed for PPM since the parser derives it

encoding_notes.pix_fmt: Add -pix_fmt yuv420p for H.264 in MP4. Without it, an RGB input may select yuv444p, which many players and browsers refuse.
encoding_notes.color_range: Add -color_range tv to silence 'Color range not set' and make the range explicit.
encoding_notes.faststart: -movflags +faststart moves the MP4 index to the front so the file streams before it is fully downloaded.
encoding_notes.bitrate_for_synthetic: Procedural gradients compress far better than camera footage. About 0.08 bits per pixel per second is visually clean, roughly 4.4 Mbps at 1280x720x60.
encoding_notes.gif: GIF needs a palette stage or it quantises to a default palette and gradients band badly. One pass: -filter_complex "split[a][b];[a]palettegen=stats_mode=diff[p];[b][p]paletteuse=dither=bayer:bayer_scale=3"
encoding_notes.lossless_intermediate: -c:v ffv1 -level 3 -pix_fmt rgb24 in .mkv, for regrading without re-rendering.
encoding_notes.encoder_availability: A minimal build has no H.264 encoder unless an external library or a platform encoder is enabled. On macOS, h264_videotoolbox needs no external dependency. Otherwise libx264 (GPL), or fall back to the native mpeg4 encoder.

building_a_minimal_ffmpeg.why: Keeps the dependency surface to the C library plus a platform encoder, and guarantees the ppm_pipe demuxer exists.
notes: --disable-autodetect refuses every optional external library, so the build cannot silently pick up whatever happens to be installed. That is what makes it reproducible.

--enable-zlib must be given back explicitly, because --disable-autodetect turns it off and without zlib there is no PNG encoder. This was hit in practice: still-image export failed with 'Default encoder for format image2 (codec png) is probably disabled'.
--enable-videotoolbox is macOS-only and provides h264_videotoolbox, a hardware H.264 encoder with no third-party dependency.
On x86 a full build wants nasm for hand-written assembly. On arm64 it is not required.
building_a_minimal_ffmpeg.no_make_install_needed: The binaries are usable in place at ffmpeg/ffmpeg and ffmpeg/ffprobe.

version_pinning.rule: The ffmpeg revision is pinned in ffmpeg.lock and `make ffmpeg` refuses to build anything else.
version_pinning.why: `git clone --depth 1` takes whatever HEAD happens to be that day, so two machines building a month apart get different decoders. This project's numbers -- frame timing, reconstruction error -- are the deliverable, and they are only comparable across runs if the decoder is identical.
version_pinning.ffprobe: ffprobe has no repository of its own; it is built from the same tree, so one pin covers both binaries. Verified: both report git-2026-08-03-9862dd8.
version_pinning.verification_placement: The check is a phony prerequisite, not part of the build rule. Folded into the rule it is skipped whenever the binary already exists -- exactly the case where a checkout has drifted off the pin.
version_pinning.moving_the_pin: `make ffmpeg-update` is deliberately separate: changing the decoder changes measured output, so it must never happen as a side effect of `make`.
